Job Title: Quantitative Data Scientist (Modeling and Feature Engineering)Location: New York, NY (In-person) Experience: 2+ yearsCompensation: $80,000-$135,000 base salary + equity
Company Overview: ShotQuality is a leader in AI-driven sports data extraction, combining advanced computer vision and data science to transform video feeds into granular player tracking data and predictive insights. Originally built around basketball, our technology now scales across football, baseball, tennis, and more, powering multi-sport analytics at the enterprise level. Our proprietary models are trusted by industry leaders, enabling sportsbooks, prediction markets, trading firms, and media companies to make confident, data-driven decisions. With 20,000+ games processed across 15+ leagues, ShotQuality turns raw video into actionable intelligence. As we expand our AI and computer vision capabilities, we continue to push the boundaries of real-time sports analytics, delivering the infrastructure that powers the future of data in sports.We are a small team in New York where the work you ship shows up in live products within days, not months.
Job Overview: We are hiring a Quantitative Data Scientist to build the features and predictive models behind ShotQuality's real-time sports products. You will turn raw event, tracking, and market data into signals, test whether they improve on market prices, and get the ones that work into production. This role sits between our data science team and our live products, so you will see your models used in real time by market-facing clients during live games. The ideal candidate comes from a sports and trading background and is energized by fast-moving markets.
Responsibilities:Feature Engineering: Design, build, and maintain features from play-by-play, player tracking, and pricing data that improve predictive accuracy.Predictive Modeling: Develop and refine probability models for in-game and pregame outcomes, with a focus on calibration and real-world performance.Market Analysis: Study how prices move around in-game events and identify where our models add information beyond current market prices.Backtesting and Evaluation: Build rigorous backtests that measure whether a model or signal holds up out of sample, against closing lines and live market prices.Research to Production: Partner with engineering to move models from notebook to live, low-latency pipelines, and monitor them once they are running.Performance Analysis: Track model performance over time, diagnose drift or degradation, and report findings clearly to leadership.Client Support: Handle requests from sophisticated, market-facing clients with fast, well-reasoned analysis.
The Role is for Candidates Who: Have a background in trading, market making, or quantitative research and get excited about finding an edge in live marketsHave built predictive models that were evaluated on real outcomes and real prices, not just a held-out test setEnjoy the feature engineering grind and can explain which features mattered and whyThink in probabilities and expected value, and care about calibration, not just accuracyMove fast, ship quickly, and iterate based on what the data showsAdapt quickly when priorities shift and are comfortable working without a fixed playbookAre comfortable with unstructured hours that follow the sports calendar, including live games on nights and weekends
The Role is NOT for Candidates Who:Have only coursework or Kaggle-style modeling experienceAren't genuinely interested in prediction markets and the sports betting spacePrefer pure research with no path to productionNeed a rigid structure or a predictable 9-to-5 scheduleAre looking for a fully remote role
Requirements:2+ years of professional experience in quantitative research, trading, or data science, ideally at a trading firm, sportsbook, or prediction marketStrong foundation in statistics and probability, including model calibration and evaluationProficiency in Python (pandas, TensorFlow, NumPy, scikit-learn or similar) and SQLHands-on experience with gradient boosting, regression, and time-series or sequential modelingExperience designing backtests and avoiding leakage and overfittingAbility to communicate results clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholdersBachelor's degree in Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Economics, or a related quantitative fieldWillingness to be available during some nights and weekends of live games (as necessary)
Nice to Have:Experience with pricing, market making, or market microstructure in sports betting or prediction marketsA track record of building and running your own models in live marketsExperience with sports data, player tracking data, or play-by-play dataExperience deploying models to real-time or low-latency systemsExposure to AWS or GCP, Docker, and workflow orchestration tools

Job Overview

OPEN TO ALL QUALIFIED US CITIZENS.

This announcement will be accepting candidate submissions until 11:45 EST, 31 October 2026.

The Information and Spectrum Warfare Directorate (RF), Information Systems Division (RFC) seeks to hire two entry – mid level, DR-0I/DR-02, Computer Scientists or Computer/Electronics Engineers, for the Resilient Networking branch, located in Rome New York. The incumbent will serve as a Research Computer Scientist/Engineer conducting basic, applied, and advanced technology development in next-generation, high-performance, and resilient tactical communication and networking technologies. The successful candidate will join an agile research and development team focused on solving critical Department of the Air Force and DoW communication challenges.

Position Duties Include, But Not Limited To

 Conduct research, design, implementation, and benchmarking of robust, fault-tolerant networking protocols, distributed systems algorithms, and routing architectures.  Develop, test, and integrate Software-Defined Radio (SDR) waveforms, protocol stacks, and network controllers utilizing C, C++, Python, and Linux-based platforms.  Design, build, and execute automated network emulation, Software-In-the-Loop (SIL), and Hardware-In-the-Loop (HIL) laboratory experiments to evaluate throughput, latency, and resiliency metrics under dynamic topologies and interference.  Participate in multidisciplinary project teams, collaborate with internal and external research partners across DoW, academia, and industry, and contribute technical findings to DoW technical reports, conference presentations, and journal papers.  Maintain laboratory hardware and software testbeds, participate in field testing events, and perform other duties as assigned. 

Required Qualifications

 United States Citizenship.  Ability to obtain and maintain Secret or Top Secret security clearance  This is a drug testing designated position. The incumbent is subject to random testing  Males must be registered for Selective Service, see www.sss.gov  Applicants must be able to meet the OPM Qualification Standards of the position being filled  S&E candidates must possess a professional science or engineering (S&E) degree from an ABET accredited academic institution  If selected at the DR-02 level, you must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the DR-01 or GS-11 level (or equivalent pay system). Specialized Experience is experience directly related to the position that was performed at a level equivalent to the grade directly below the position  This is an APDP position requiring completion of Level/Tier 1 (Foundational) or Level/Tier 2 (Practitioner) certification within Engineering &Technology Management (ETM). Selectee will have 5 years to meet the APDP certification requirements of the position. 

Desired Qualifications

 MS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or Electrical Engineering with a focus on communications and networking.  Hands-on experience with Software-Defined Radio (SDR) platforms (e.g., USRP/Ettus Research, HackRF, bladeRF) and frameworks (e.g., GNU Radio, RFNoC, REDHAWK).  Working knowledge of digital signal processing (DSP) concepts, physical layer modulation schemes, and wireless communications fundamentals.  Experience utilizing MATLAB / Simulink for communications system modeling, protocol simulation, or signal analysis.  Experience applying Artificial Intelligence / Machine Learning (AI/ML) techniques (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow, Scikit-learn) to networking, cognitive radio, traffic classification, or spectrum monitoring.  Familiarity with network modeling, discrete-event simulation, and emulation platforms such as ns-3, CORE, EMANE.  Experience with Linux kernel networking, eBPF, network namespaces, containerization (Docker, Podman), and distributed version control (Git).  Understanding of military communications systems, tactical data links, or mobile ad-hoc networks (MANETs).  Demonstrated ability to communicate complex technical concepts effectively in written reports and technical briefings.  Willingness to collaborate in cross-functional teams involving government scientists, military operators, and contractor personnel. 

Proficiency In The Following Is Strongly Desired

 Development and debugging of software in C, C++, and/or Python within a native Linux development environment.  Practical understanding of fundamental networking concepts, the OSI/TCP-IP reference models, routing algorithms, socket programming, and protocol analysis tools (e.g., Wireshark, tcpdump).  Implementation of algorithms, data structures, and multi-threaded or event-driven software architectures.  Ability to operate effectively within an iterative research, development, and laboratory demonstration environment. 

Telework

Yes, this position is eligible for situational telework; as determined by agency policy

rows.title: AI Software Engineer

parsed.text: New York City, NY, United States

rows.descriptionText:
Applied AI Scientist — Agentic Decision Systems

Location: Canada or United States (US time zones)

Experience: Typically 2+ years of relevant applied work, although we care substantially more about the quality and difficulty of the problems you have solved than the number of years you have been solving them.

About The Role

We are looking for exceptional quantitative thinkers to build agentic systems that help people make better decisions.

This is not primarily a conventional data science role, an LLM application-development role, or a prompt-engineering role. We are interested in people who want to understand how intelligent systems can reason over complex problems, use tools and models effectively, learn from evidence, and become systematically better over time.

A Central Question In This Role Is

How do we make an agentic system measurably better at the decisions it is intended to support?

That means moving beyond intuition, demos and prompt alchemy. You will think about objectives, observability, feedback, evaluation datasets, statistical uncertainty, experiments, simulation, failure modes and improvement loops. You should be interested not only in building agents, but in developing rigorous ways for those agents—and the systems around them—to improve.

You will work on ambiguous, consequential enterprise problems where the answer is rarely “use an LLM.” Sometimes the right solution will involve an agent. Sometimes it will involve statistical modelling, optimization, machine learning, simulation, rules, or a surprisingly simple piece of mathematics. Frequently it will involve several of these working together.

We want people who are technically ambitious, intellectually demanding, empirically minded and impatient with hand-waving.

What You Will Do

Design and build agentic decision-support systems that can reason over data, interact with tools and models, maintain state, decompose complex problems and support consequential human decisions.Develop mechanisms for systematic improvement. Design evaluation frameworks, feedback loops, benchmarks, experiments and instrumentation that allow us to determine where a system fails, why it fails and whether a proposed change genuinely improves it.Turn “make the agent better” into a quantitative problem. Define measurable objectives and failure modes; build representative test sets; analyze performance distributions rather than anecdotes; and distinguish real improvement from movement on a convenient metric.Explore self-improving agentic architectures. This may involve reflection and critique, adaptive tool or model selection, memory, search, planning, generated training/evaluation data, policy improvement, human feedback, simulation or other mechanisms. We are interested in what works—not in allegiance to a particular architecture.Bring statistical and machine-learning judgment to agentic systems. Use probabilistic modelling, statistical inference, ML, optimization or causal reasoning when they make the system more useful, more reliable or easier to improve.Generate high-quality software using AI coding systems. We expect you to work AI-natively. The objective is not to demonstrate how quickly you can type Python; it is to produce excellent software.Own difficult problems end to end. Work from an initially ambiguous business or decision problem through problem formulation, system design, implementation, evaluation and deployment.Challenge the problem definition. A technically sophisticated solution to the wrong problem is still the wrong solution. You should be comfortable questioning assumptions and reframing what is being optimized.Work directly with senior technical and business stakeholders. Explain complex ideas precisely without hiding behind jargon, and make uncertainty, assumptions and limitations explicit.

What We Are Looking For

Exceptional quantitative foundations

You have rigorous training in a highly quantitative discipline such as mathematics, physics, statistics, engineering, econometrics, operations research or another discipline involving substantial mathematical and quantitative reasoning.

A master's or PhD is welcome, but neither is a substitute for evidence of unusually strong analytical thinking. Exceptional candidates with a bachelor's degree are equally of interest.

You should be comfortable reasoning mathematically about unfamiliar problems rather than relying solely on methods you have used before.

Experience with agentic systems

You have meaningful hands-on experience designing or developing agentic systems.

We are particularly interested in experience involving some combination of:

multi-step reasoning and planning;structured outputs and stateful workflows;memory and context management;multi-agent or decomposed-agent architectures;agent evaluation;automated critique or refinement;feedback-driven adaptation;decision-support applications; andmechanisms intended to improve system performance over repeated iterations.

A chatbot with a system prompt is not, for our purposes, substantial experience building an agentic system. Neither is wrapping an LLM around a vector database and calling the result an agent.

Statistical and machine-learning literacy

You do not need to be a specialist in every branch of machine learning, but you should have enough statistical maturity to reason properly about evidence.

We expect practical familiarity with statistical modelling and machine learning and, more importantly, sound instincts around:

uncertainty;validation;sampling and selection effects;overfitting;experiment design;measurement;predictive versus causal claims;distribution shift; anddetermining whether a system actually works.

You should instinctively ask what the comparison is, how performance is being measured, whether the evaluation resembles the real problem, and how confident we should be in the result.

AI-native software engineering

You are extremely effective at producing software, but we do not equate software engineering ability with manually writing large quantities of code.

We expect you to use state-of-the-art coding agents extensively—potentially for essentially all implementations.

What matters is whether you can make those systems produce excellent code.

You Should Be Capable Of

designing a coherent software architecture before or while implementation emerges;decomposing work effectively for coding agents;inspecting and interrogating unfamiliar generated code;identifying bad abstractions, subtle bugs and unnecessary complexity;designing meaningful tests rather than merely achieving test coverage;maintaining reproducible environments;understanding APIs, data pipelines and production system boundaries;debugging systems whose implementation you did not personally type; andleaving behind code that another strong engineer can understand, extend and trust.

You are accountable for every line you ship even if you personally typed none of them.

The Intellectual Style We Value

The strongest candidates for this role tend to have several things in common.

They are deeply curious but difficult to impress. They enjoy abstraction, but they want abstractions to survive contact with data. They are happy to propose an ambitious architecture and equally happy to discard it when a simpler system performs better. They distinguish a compelling demonstration from convincing evidence. They are interested in why something works, where it stops working, and what experiment would distinguish competing explanations. They are willing to use LLMs aggressively without anthropomorphizing them or treating their behavior as magic. And when someone says, “This version feels better,” their instinct is to ask: “Better according to what measurement?”

You Will Probably Not Enjoy This Role If

Most of your interest is in conventional analytics, dashboards or notebook-based data science.Your experience with generative AI is primarily prompting, chatbot development or basic RAG applications.You prefer selecting an AI framework and following its abstractions to thinking from first principles about the underlying system.You regard agent behaviour as too unpredictable to evaluate quantitatively or you are satisfied with qualitative demonstrations when controlled measurement is possible.You believe increasingly elaborate agent architectures are inherently more intelligent.You enjoy writing code but are uncomfortable delegating implementation to AI systems.Conversely, you use AI-generated code without wanting to understand its architecture, test its assumptions or take responsibility for its quality.You need requirements to be fully specified before you can make progress.

Particularly Interesting, But Not Required

Experience with one or more of the following would be especially valuable:

decision science, causal inference, Bayesian modelling or optimization;reinforcement learning, contextual bandits, simulation or adaptive experimentation;agent evaluation, observability, benchmark construction or synthetic task generation;inference-time search, test-time computation, model routing or ensemble systems;human-in-the-loop or production agent architectures; andcomplex enterprise decision environments such as financial services, insurance, supply chain or logistics.

The role is product-oriented: you will shape the capabilities, workflows and evaluation systems that make our agentic products more useful, reliable and improvable.

You will turn difficult enterprise problems, user needs and client lessons into reusable product capabilities. Working with technical, product, domain and client-facing teams, you will identify high-leverage problems, formulate improvement hypotheses, and design experiments that distinguish genuine progress from superficial gains.

We expect you to move quickly from ideas to prototypes and measurable evidence without compromising reasoning, quality or technical integrity. The goal is not to build the most elaborate AI system, but products that make better decisions, whose performance we can understand, and which we know how to improve.

About Mphasis

Mphasis applies next-generation technology to help enterprises transform their businesses globally. Our work combines technology, domain expertise and applied innovation to solve complex problems for enterprise clients.

Equal Opportunity

Mphasis is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified candidates are considered without regard to characteristics protected by applicable federal, state, provincial or local law. Mphasis is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities throughout the recruitment process.

rows.descriptionText:
Position Title: AI Agent Developer

Location: New York, NY (Hybrid – 3 days onsite, 2 days remote)

Clearance Requirements: Not specified

Position Status: Contract through June 30, 2027 (potential extension)

Pay Rate: $40–$48 per hour (W2), depending on experience

Position Description

We are seeking an AI Agent Developer to help build, test, and support enterprise conversational AI agents and the web applications that power them. This opportunity is ideal for developers interested in generative AI, intelligent automation, cloud technologies, and full-stack development.

You will collaborate with experienced engineers to develop conversational AI solutions using Google Cloud Platform (GCP) and Dialogflow CX, integrate AI agents with Microsoft Azure and ServiceNow, build responsive web interfaces, and support automated testing and CI/CD pipelines.

This hybrid contract opportunity offers hands-on exposure to enterprise AI development, large-scale integrations, and modern software engineering practices.

Work arrangement: Hybrid, with three days onsite and two days remote per week in New York, NY.

Interview process: First round via Microsoft Teams; second round onsite in New York, NY.

Key Responsibilities

Conversational AI and Backend Development

Build, configure, and test conversational flows, intents, route groups, and LLM-powered tools using Dialogflow CX.

Contribute to AI agent development using Google's Agent Development Kit (ADK) and related frameworks.

Develop and maintain REST APIs, webhooks, and backend services using Python, with exposure to .NET or Node.js.

Integrate conversational AI agents with enterprise platforms, including ServiceNow and Microsoft Azure.

Write SQL queries to support agent lookups, reporting, and conversational analytics.

Front-End and Web Application Development

Develop responsive, accessible web interfaces using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and TypeScript.

Work with modern front-end frameworks such as React or Angular.

Integrate web components with backend services and AI agent APIs.

Implement browser-based session handling, loading states, and error handling.

Support internal dashboards, analytics pages, testing tools, and administrative interfaces.

Testing, DevOps, and Delivery

Maintain and improve Azure DevOps CI/CD pipelines for agent configurations, backend services, and front-end applications.

Update YAML pipeline configurations with appropriate engineering review.

Develop and execute unit tests, API tests, conversational flow regression tests, and front-end component tests.

Troubleshoot software defects, investigate failed test runs, document findings, and escalate issues when necessary.

Participate in Agile ceremonies, including sprint planning, daily standups, backlog refinement, and Program Increment (PI) planning within a SAFe environment.

Maintain technical documentation, API specifications, agent flow designs, and operational runbooks.

Required Skills/Education

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Python Programming Proficiency Is Required.

Working knowledge of .NET and front-end technologies, including HTML, CSS, JavaScript, or TypeScript.

Understanding of REST APIs, JSON, webhooks, browser-based API integration, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

Basic to intermediate SQL query-writing skills.

Experience using Git and a modern IDE, such as Visual Studio Code.

Exposure to unit testing frameworks such as PyTest, Jest, or xUnit.

Strong analytical, troubleshooting, written communication, and collaboration skills.

Willingness to learn, ask questions, accept feedback, and work collaboratively with senior engineers.

Experience level: 0–8 years of relevant experience.

Preferred Qualifications

Hands-on exposure to Dialogflow CX, conversational AI, chatbots, generative AI, or LLM-powered applications; academic projects and personal projects are welcome.

Familiarity with Google's Agent Development Kit (ADK) or other AI agent development frameworks.

Basic understanding of prompt engineering, intent classification, and conversational design.

Exposure to front-end testing tools such as Jest, Selenium, Playwright, or Cypress.

Familiarity with Azure DevOps, CI/CD pipelines, Git repositories, and automated deployment processes.

Exposure to .NET/C#, ServiceNow REST APIs, or ServiceNow Flow Designer.

Understanding of OAuth 2.0, API keys, secrets management, CORS, and cross-site scripting (XSS) prevention.

Awareness of Agile and SAFe development practices.

Familiarity with Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, or infrastructure as code.

Exposure to serverless platforms such as Google Cloud Run or Azure Functions, or Contact Center AI (CCAI).

Interest in site reliability engineering (SRE), observability, monitoring, and AIOps.

Technology Stack

AI and Cloud: Google Cloud Platform (GCP), Dialogflow CX, Google Agent Development Kit (ADK), Microsoft Azure

Backend: Python 3.x, .NET/C#, Node.js, REST APIs, webhooks

Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Angular

Data: SQL, JSON, conversational analytics

DevOps and Testing: Azure DevOps, YAML pipelines, Git, PyTest, Jest, xUnit, API and UI testing

Enterprise Integration: ServiceNow REST APIs, Flow Designer

Agile and Development Tools: SAFe, Jira, Azure Boards, Visual Studio Code

About Seneca Resources

At Seneca Resources, we are more than just a staffing and consulting firm, we are a trusted career partner. With offices across the U.S. and clients ranging from Fortune 500 companies to government organizations, we provide opportunities that help professionals grow their careers while making an impact.

When you work with Seneca, you’re choosing a company that invests in your success, celebrates your achievements, and connects you to meaningful work with leading organizations nationwide. We take the time to understand your goals and match you with roles that align with your skills and career path. Our consultants and contractors enjoy competitive pay, comprehensive health, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) retirement plans, and the support of a dedicated team who will advocate for you every step of the way.

Seneca Resources is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace where all qualified individuals are encouraged to apply.

rows.title: Engineer II, Systems Engineering
rows.descriptionText:
Controls Engineer – New Product Development

About Motivair

Motivair by Schneider Electric is a leading provider of advanced liquid cooling technologies and intelligent controls systems designed for hyperscale data centers, high-performance computing (HPC), AI infrastructure, and other mission-critical environments. Our engineering teams develop innovative thermal management solutions that help customers improve efficiency, reliability, scalability, and sustainability in the world's most demanding digital applications.

As part of our New Product Development organization, you will collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to create next-generation cooling platforms and control systems that support the rapid growth of AI and data center technologies.

Position Summary

The Controls Engineer is responsible for the design, development, programming, integration, and validation of control systems for Motivair's liquid cooling products. This role combines controls engineering, embedded software development, system integration, and product innovation to deliver reliable, scalable, and customer-focused solutions.

The ideal candidate possesses strong technical expertise in industrial automation, PLC programming, communication protocols, and control system architecture, along with the ability to work collaboratively across engineering, manufacturing, and customer-facing teams throughout the product lifecycle.

Key Responsibilities

Develop, program, test, and troubleshoot PLC logic, HMI interfaces, and control algorithms for liquid cooling systems.Design and implement automation architectures incorporating sensors, pumps, valves, VFDs, instrumentation, and communication networks.Create and maintain electrical and controls documentation, including I/O lists, control narratives, functional specifications, wiring diagrams, and test procedures.Configure and validate industrial communication protocols including Modbus, BACnet, SNMP, and Ethernet-based networks.Participate in the development of embedded control solutions and integrated control architectures for new product platforms.Collaborate with mechanical, electrical, manufacturing, quality, and service teams to ensure successful product development and deployment.Support system testing, Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), commissioning, and field startup activities.Analyze and troubleshoot hardware, software, and controls-related issues throughout the product lifecycle.Translate customer requirements, technical specifications, and industry standards into effective controls solutions.Support continuous improvement initiatives, software standardization, platform scalability, and development of reusable controls frameworks.Contribute to technology roadmaps and future product innovations supporting AI and data center cooling applications.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Controls Engineering, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical discipline.Minimum 5 years of experience in industrial automation, controls engineering, embedded systems, or a related field.Experience developing and troubleshooting PLC applications utilizing Ladder Logic (LD), Structured Text (ST), and Function Block Diagrams (FBD).Experience with BMS, SCADA, or industrial automation environments.Strong knowledge of industrial communication protocols such as Modbus, BACnet, and SNMP.Understanding of control theory, instrumentation, PID control, and system integration principles.Ability to read and interpret electrical schematics, P&IDs, control panel drawings, and system architecture documentation.Experience performing system validation, troubleshooting, and root-cause analysis.Strong organizational and project management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities.Excellent communication skills and ability to collaborate effectively within cross-functional teams.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with Schneider Electric EcoStruxure platforms, Modicon PLCs, Carel controls, C.Suite, 1Tool, or similar industrial automation platforms.Experience developing embedded software or firmware using C, C++, Python, or related programming languages.Knowledge of liquid cooling systems, thermal management technologies, HVAC systems, or fluid process controls.Experience integrating VFDs, pumps, heat exchangers, and fieldbus-connected devices.Familiarity with Git, GitHub, or other software version control systems.Experience with cloud-connected architectures, analytics platforms, and remote monitoring technologies.Knowledge of cybersecurity principles for industrial control systems and operational technology environments.Experience supporting data center, hyperscale, mission-critical, or AI infrastructure applications.Exposure to digital twin technologies, simulation tools, and virtual commissioning environments.Understanding of Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DFMA), Lean Engineering, and standardized controls architecture methodologies.

What You'll Gain

Opportunity to develop next-generation cooling technologies supporting AI and hyperscale data center growth.Exposure to cutting-edge automation, controls, and digital infrastructure technologies.Collaboration with world-class engineering teams across Schneider Electric and Motivair.Professional development, training, and career growth opportunities within a global technology leader.The ability to directly influence products that help customers achieve sustainability and efficiency goals.

Why Schneider Electric?

Schneider Electric is leading the digital transformation of energy management and automation. At Motivair, you'll play a critical role in developing innovative cooling and controls technologies that enable the future of AI, cloud computing, and mission-critical infrastructure. We foster a culture of innovation, collaboration, inclusion, and continuous learning, empowering our employees to make a meaningful impact on a more sustainable world.

At Schneider, we believe that every employee is a talent who deserves equal opportunities. This means you matter. Every individual needs to feel valued, supported, and treated fairly to do their best work.

Our Total Rewards is our way of saying: “We see you. We value you”. It’s more than just pay and benefits- it’s a meaningful investment in you. It is designed for you to perform, grow, feel safe, and elevate your potential to shine as an impact maker.

For this U.S. based position, the expected pay range is USD 86,400 - USD 129,600 per year. This pay range includes base pay and short-term incentives. The compensation range for this full-time position applies to candidates located within the United States. Our pay ranges are determined by reviewing roles of similar responsibility and level. Within the pay range, individual pay is determined by several factors including performance, knowledge, job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

Schneider Electric is there when it matters most to you

Our Total Rewards package outlines all the benefits and support you’ll enjoy as part of the Schneider Electric team:

Care for Yourself and Your Family. rows.descriptionText:
Company Description Rosco Vision, founded in 1907 and based in Jamaica, NY, is a leading supplier of backup camera systems, mirrors, visors, and visual safety solutions for commercial vehicles across North America and worldwide. The company engineers and manufactures visual safety systems for a wide range of fleet vehicles, including being the largest supplier of mirror systems to the North American school bus market. Rosco Vision serves major OEMs and parts distributors such as Navistar/IC Corp., Freightliner/Thomas Built, Blue Bird, and AM General. Its products are developed from real-world understanding of driver challenges and are designed to support fleet managers in running efficient, safe, and compliant operations. Team members contribute to solutions that directly impact road safety and regulatory compliance for commercial fleets.
Role Description This is a full-time, on-site Computer Numerical Control (CNC) Programmer role located in Jamaica, NY. The CNC Programmer will create, modify, and optimize CNC programs for machining parts used in Rosco Vision’s safety systems, ensuring accuracy, efficiency, and adherence to engineering specifications. Day-to-day responsibilities include interpreting technical drawings, selecting appropriate tools and machining methods, setting up and testing CNC equipment, and troubleshooting program or machining issues. The role involves collaborating with engineering, production, and quality teams to improve manufacturing processes, reduce waste, and maintain high product standards. The CNC Programmer will also maintain documentation, follow safety procedures, and support continuous improvement initiatives in the machine shop.

 Candidates should possess strong CNC Programming and Programming skills for creating and optimizing machine instructions.Candidates should possess Machining and Milling skills for operating and fine-tuning CNC equipment and processes.Candidates should possess Technical Drawing skills for reading and interpreting blueprints, CAD models, and engineering specifications.Experience with CNC controllers (e.g., Fanuc, Haas, or similar) and CAM/CAD software is beneficial.Knowledge of materials, cutting tools, feeds and speeds, and shop math is preferred.Attention to detail, problem-solving ability, and adherence to safety and quality standards are essential.Prior experience in a manufacturing or industrial environment, ideally in automotive or commercial vehicle components, is an advantage.A relevant technical diploma, certification, or equivalent practical experience in CNC programming or machining is desirable.

rows.descriptionText:
RIT's Department of Computer Engineering invites applications from highly motivated individuals looking to join a vibrant community of teacher-scholars as a tenure-track faculty member at the rank of Assistant Professor. Successful candidates are expected to build a strong externally-funded research program, advise Ph.D. and master's students, develop and teach undergraduate and graduate classes, advise undergraduate researchers and design teams, and work collaboratively to advance the goals of the department. We are currently seeking candidates with research expertise in one or more of the following areas: Machine Learning and Edge AI, Heterogeneous Computing, Networking and IoT, Quantum Computing.

We are seeking an individual who has the ability and interest in contributing to a community committed to student-centeredness; professional development and scholarship; integrity and ethics; respect, innovation and flexibility; and teamwork and collaboration. Select to view links to RIT's core values, honor code, and commitment to community statement.

Salary Range: $100,000 - $130,000

The College/ Department

The Computer Engineering Department is one of six academic departments in the Kate Gleason College of Engineering. The Kate Gleason College of Engineering | RIT offers bachelor's and master's in biomedical engineering, chemical engineering, computer engineering, electrical engineering, industrial engineering, mechanical engineering, and microelectronics engineering as well as four Ph.D. degrees in biomedical and chemical engineering, electrical and computer engineering, mechanical and industrial engineering, and microsystems engineering and additional master's programs in engineering management and leadership. Serving over 2600 undergraduates and 400 graduate students, the college is committed to growing its research profile while maintaining a strong commitment to undergraduate education. Major research themes include advanced manufacturing; biomedical and healthcare engineering; artificial intelligence and machine learning; cyber-physical systems; micro- and nanoscale systems devices and materials; energy and environment; and data analysis modeling and simulation. Hallmarks of the undergraduate experience include one full year of cooperative education, an innovative multidisciplinary senior design program, and an impressive variety of well-supported student teams and clubs.

The Computer Engineering Department has about four hundred and fifty undergraduates, one hundred graduate students, and eighteen faculty and staff. The department is known for its outstanding curricula, career-oriented education, collaborative research and state-of-the-art laboratories and computing facilities. Faculty members are actively engaged in research, innovative teaching, and partnerships with industry, and participate in the Electrical and Computer Engineering Ph.D. and cross-disciplinary Ph.D. programs in Computing and Information Sciences, Microsystems Engineering, and Imaging Science. For more information, visit https://www.rit.edu/kgcoe/computerengineering/.

The University And Rochester Community

Rochester Institute of Technology is home to leading creators, entrepreneurs, innovators, and researchers. The university enrolls 16,868 undergraduates and 2,904 graduate students in more than 200 programs, and across nine academic colleges, five international campuses, as well as other degree-granting units, placing it among some of the largest private universities in the U.S. RIT is internationally recognized and ranked for academic leadership in business, computing, engineering, imaging science, liberal arts, sustainability, and fine and applied arts. RIT is also home to the National Technical Institute for the Deaf, the world's first and largest technological college for deaf and hard-of-hearing students. With more than 900 students from around the world, NTID offers unparalleled support services for deaf and hard-of-hearing students. RIT's cooperative education program is one of the oldest and largest in the nation. The university revised its 2025 strategic plan, Greatness Through Difference, in the fall of 2018. The plan leverages RIT's unique history with a renewed focus on using the interdisciplinary power of technology, the arts, and design to shape the future and the world.

In 2019, RIT moved into the high research activity institution or "R2" category under the updated Carnegie Classification of Institutions of Higher Learning, ranking it among the top six percent of colleges and universities in the nation for research activity. U.S. News and World Report (USNWR) now ranks RIT No. 105 in its "National Universities" category, and No. 54 and No. 63 for Best Undergraduate and Graduate Engineering Programs, respectively. The publication also ranks RIT No. 11 in the U.S. for co-op or internship programs, No. 48 among best-value schools, and No. 41 among most innovative. Sponsored research awards totaled $92 million in the fiscal year 2022, up from $78 million in 2018. Today, RIT counts nearly 140,000 alumni around the world. Its endowment is currently valued at $1.257 billion, and the university benefits from sound financial management.

Always on the cutting edge, RIT's educational programs continue to evolve to meet the needs of today's students. Building on its legacy of excellence across STEM and the arts and its commitment to developing creative thinkers, RIT launched the Performing Arts Scholars program in 2019. In the fall of 2022, 482 first-year students accepted scholarships to join this program, regardless of major, bringing the total number of PA Scholars to 1,400. In support of this programming, RIT is unveiling the Student Hall for Exploration and Development (SHED) in the fall of 2023, with major facilities for the performing arts, and new classrooms, surrounding an enormous multi-story core of maker spaces. RIT has also launched a series of very successful Combined Accelerated Bachelor's/Master's Degree (CAB-M) programs, which attracted about 750 students in the fall of 2022. In addition, RIT is developing a large suite of online programs with an emphasis on upskilling for adult learners through its offerings at RIT Certified.

Qualifications

 Doctorate in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering or closely related fieldAbility and commitment to effectively teach and mentor undergraduate and graduate students Record of disseminating scholarly research in refereed (peer-reviewed) publications Demonstrated evidence of experience or potential to establish an independent externally-sponsored research programExpertise in the areas of Edge AI, Heterogeneous Computing, Networking and IoT, and/or Quantum Computing.Excellent communication skillsAbility to contribute in meaningful ways to the university's continuing commitment to cultural diversity, pluralism and individual differences.Interest in working in a collaborative, collegial environment

Position Description

We are seeking an AI Agent Developer to help build, test, and support enterprise conversational AI agents and the web applications that power them. This opportunity is ideal for developers interested in generative AI, intelligent automation, cloud technologies, and full-stack development.

You will collaborate with experienced engineers to develop conversational AI solutions using Google Cloud Platform (GCP) and Dialogflow CX, integrate AI agents with Microsoft Azure and ServiceNow, build responsive web interfaces, and support automated testing and CI/CD pipelines.

This hybrid contract opportunity offers hands-on exposure to enterprise AI development, large-scale integrations, and modern software engineering practices.

Work arrangement: Hybrid, with three days onsite and two days remote per week in New York, NY.

Interview process: First round via Microsoft Teams; second round onsite in New York, NY.

Key Responsibilities

Conversational AI and Backend Development

Build, configure, and test conversational flows, intents, route groups, and LLM-powered tools using Dialogflow CX.

Contribute to AI agent development using Google's Agent Development Kit (ADK) and related frameworks.

Develop and maintain REST APIs, webhooks, and backend services using Python, with exposure to .NET or Node.js.

Integrate conversational AI agents with enterprise platforms, including ServiceNow and Microsoft Azure.

Write SQL queries to support agent lookups, reporting, and conversational analytics.

Front-End and Web Application Development

Develop responsive, accessible web interfaces using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and TypeScript.

Work with modern front-end frameworks such as React or Angular.

Integrate web components with backend services and AI agent APIs.

Implement browser-based session handling, loading states, and error handling.

Support internal dashboards, analytics pages, testing tools, and administrative interfaces.

Testing, DevOps, and Delivery

Maintain and improve Azure DevOps CI/CD pipelines for agent configurations, backend services, and front-end applications.

Update YAML pipeline configurations with appropriate engineering review.

Develop and execute unit tests, API tests, conversational flow regression tests, and front-end component tests.

Troubleshoot software defects, investigate failed test runs, document findings, and escalate issues when necessary.

Participate in Agile ceremonies, including sprint planning, daily standups, backlog refinement, and Program Increment (PI) planning within a SAFe environment.

Maintain technical documentation, API specifications, agent flow designs, and operational runbooks.

Required Skills/Education

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Python Programming Proficiency Is Required.

Working knowledge of .NET and front-end technologies, including HTML, CSS, JavaScript, or TypeScript.

Understanding of REST APIs, JSON, webhooks, browser-based API integration, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

Basic to intermediate SQL query-writing skills.

Experience using Git and a modern IDE, such as Visual Studio Code.

Exposure to unit testing frameworks such as PyTest, Jest, or xUnit.

Strong analytical, troubleshooting, written communication, and collaboration skills.

Willingness to learn, ask questions, accept feedback, and work collaboratively with senior engineers.

Experience level: 0–8 years of relevant experience.

Preferred Qualifications

Hands-on exposure to Dialogflow CX, conversational AI, chatbots, generative AI, or LLM-powered applications; academic projects and personal projects are welcome.

Familiarity with Google's Agent Development Kit (ADK) or other AI agent development frameworks.

Basic understanding of prompt engineering, intent classification, and conversational design.

Exposure to front-end testing tools such as Jest, Selenium, Playwright, or Cypress.

Familiarity with Azure DevOps, CI/CD pipelines, Git repositories, and automated deployment processes.

Exposure to .NET/C#, ServiceNow REST APIs, or ServiceNow Flow Designer.

Understanding of OAuth 2.0, API keys, secrets management, CORS, and cross-site scripting (XSS) prevention.

Awareness of Agile and SAFe development practices.

Familiarity with Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, or infrastructure as code.

Exposure to serverless platforms such as Google Cloud Run or Azure Functions, or Contact Center AI (CCAI).

Interest in site reliability engineering (SRE), observability, monitoring, and AIOps.

Technology Stack

AI and Cloud: Google Cloud Platform (GCP), Dialogflow CX, Google Agent Development Kit (ADK), Microsoft Azure

Backend: Python 3.x, .NET/C#, Node.js, REST APIs, webhooks

Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Angular

Data: SQL, JSON, conversational analytics

DevOps and Testing: Azure DevOps, YAML pipelines, Git, PyTest, Jest, xUnit, API and UI testing

Enterprise Integration: ServiceNow REST APIs, Flow Designer

Overview

 JOB DESCRIPTION 

The Jefferies Equity Research Data Strategy Team is a global team embedded within the Equity Research department, responsible for shaping and executing the department's data and AI strategy. On the data side, the team helps incorporate fundamental and alternative datasets into Analyst research reports, combining analysts’ domain expertise with our team’s technical skills to produce thoughtful, defensible, and actionable analysis of real-world behavior at scale. On the AI side, our team is responsible for building internal generative AI tooling along with evaluating third-party AI models and tools to enhance our analysts’ work. We help integrate AI capabilities into analysts’ daily workflows and ensure that first- and third-party datasets are fully AI-accessible to them. Statistics, data engineering, data science, and AI are cornerstones of our work.

As a Data Scientist at Jefferies, your focus will be to support the Research Analysts and the Data Strategy Team’s broader platform. The candidate will use technical and financial skills to implement ideas and requests from the Research Analysts, while also building and maintaining relationships with internal and external stakeholders, working in collaboration with the rest of the Global Data Strategy Team.

Key Responsibilities

 Query, transform, analyze, and combine large datasets in support of solving problems and implementing research ideas across sectors and data categories, occasionally developing statistical models to predict outcomes  Enhance our platform through the creation and maintenance of tools, AI agents, MCP servers, and processes that streamline, scale, and standardize our ability to evaluate, clean, analyze, and disseminate data  Contribute to the data centralization process, ensuring all first- and third-party data assets are AI-accessible and meet quality, lineage, and governance standards  Present highly technical methods to non-technical stakeholders and translate open-ended questions into data-driven insights  Maintain and build relationships with key internal and external stakeholders, including research teams, third-party data vendors, management, and possibly buy-side clients 

Qualifications

Required

 Transferable experience on the sell-side or buy-side, in data science, data research, or similar function  STEM degree with preference for Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, Statistics, Quantitative Finance, and related disciplines  Strong proficiency with Python, intermediate or better proficiency with SQL and/or Apache Spark  Experience analyzing and visualizing large datasets  Experience with AI-assisted development (Claude Code, GitHub CoPilot, Cursor, etc.)  Familiarity with LLMs, LangChain, vector databases, and RAG pipelines  Excellent communication skills with the ability to translate complex technical concepts for non-technical stakeholders 

Preferred

 Demonstrated interest in fundamental equity research and financial modelling  Experience with Databricks or Snowflake and cloud platforms such as AWS  Experience with Atlassian project management tools (JIRA, Confluence, Bitbucket)  Experience with knowledge graphs 

Primary Location Full Time Salary Range of $100,000 - $120,000.

rows.descriptionText:
Data is at the center of everything we do. As a startup, we disrupted the credit card industry by individually personalizing every credit card offer using statistical modeling and the relational database, cutting edge technology in 1988! Fast-forward a few years, and this little innovation and our passion for data has skyrocketed us to a Fortune 200 company and a leader in the world of data-driven decision-making.

As a Data Scientist at Capital One, you’ll be part of a team that’s leading the next wave of disruption at a whole new scale, using the latest in computing and machine learning technologies and operating across billions of customer records to unlock the big opportunities that help everyday people save money, time and agony in their financial lives.

Team Description

People Tech is a close-knit team of 480+ dedicated, talented and diverse individuals. Together, we're focused on delivering exceptional experiences and tech innovations for Capital One's associates and business partners. As a team, we deliver modern engineering capabilities, services, and platforms. We are the proud tech partner to the following enterprise lines of business: Brand, Corporate Development, Corporate Strategy, Experience Design, Enterprise Supplier Management, Global External Affairs, Human Resources, Legal, and Global Workplace Solutions.

In this role, you will: 

Partner with a cross-functional team of data scientists, software engineers, machine learning engineers and product managers to deliver AI powered products that change how customers interact with their money. Leverage a broad stack of technologies - Pytorch, AWS Ultraclusters, Hugging Face, LangChain, Lightning, VectorDBs, and more - to reveal the insights hidden within huge volumes of numeric and textual data. Be the expert in Natural Language Processing (NLP) to harness the power of Large Language Models (LLMs), adapt and finetune them for customer facing applications and features. Build machine learning and NLP models through all phases of development, from design through training, evaluation, and validation; partnering with engineering teams to operationalize them in scalable and resilient production systems that serve 80+ million customers. Flex your interpersonal skills to translate the complexity of your work into tangible business goals. 

The Ideal Candidate is:

Job Title: Quantitative Data Scientist (Modeling and Feature Engineering)Location: New York, NY (In-person) Experience: 2+ yearsCompensation: $80,000-$135,000 base salary + equity
Company Overview: ShotQuality is a leader in AI-driven sports data extraction, combining advanced computer vision and data science to transform video feeds into granular player tracking data and predictive insights. Originally built around basketball, our technology now scales across football, baseball, tennis, and more, powering multi-sport analytics at the enterprise level. Our proprietary models are trusted by industry leaders, enabling sportsbooks, prediction markets, trading firms, and media companies to make confident, data-driven decisions. With 20,000+ games processed across 15+ leagues, ShotQuality turns raw video into actionable intelligence. As we expand our AI and computer vision capabilities, we continue to push the boundaries of real-time sports analytics, delivering the infrastructure that powers the future of data in sports.We are a small team in New York where the work you ship shows up in live products within days, not months.
Job Overview: We are hiring a Quantitative Data Scientist to build the features and predictive models behind ShotQuality's real-time sports products. You will turn raw event, tracking, and market data into signals, test whether they improve on market prices, and get the ones that work into production. This role sits between our data science team and our live products, so you will see your models used in real time by market-facing clients during live games. The ideal candidate comes from a sports and trading background and is energized by fast-moving markets.
Responsibilities:Feature Engineering: Design, build, and maintain features from play-by-play, player tracking, and pricing data that improve predictive accuracy.Predictive Modeling: Develop and refine probability models for in-game and pregame outcomes, with a focus on calibration and real-world performance.Market Analysis: Study how prices move around in-game events and identify where our models add information beyond current market prices.Backtesting and Evaluation: Build rigorous backtests that measure whether a model or signal holds up out of sample, against closing lines and live market prices.Research to Production: Partner with engineering to move models from notebook to live, low-latency pipelines, and monitor them once they are running.Performance Analysis: Track model performance over time, diagnose drift or degradation, and report findings clearly to leadership.Client Support: Handle requests from sophisticated, market-facing clients with fast, well-reasoned analysis.
The Role is for Candidates Who: Have a background in trading, market making, or quantitative research and get excited about finding an edge in live marketsHave built predictive models that were evaluated on real outcomes and real prices, not just a held-out test setEnjoy the feature engineering grind and can explain which features mattered and whyThink in probabilities and expected value, and care about calibration, not just accuracyMove fast, ship quickly, and iterate based on what the data showsAdapt quickly when priorities shift and are comfortable working without a fixed playbookAre comfortable with unstructured hours that follow the sports calendar, including live games on nights and weekends
The Role is NOT for Candidates Who:Have only coursework or Kaggle-style modeling experienceAren't genuinely interested in prediction markets and the sports betting spacePrefer pure research with no path to productionNeed a rigid structure or a predictable 9-to-5 scheduleAre looking for a fully remote role
Requirements:2+ years of professional experience in quantitative research, trading, or data science, ideally at a trading firm, sportsbook, or prediction marketStrong foundation in statistics and probability, including model calibration and evaluationProficiency in Python (pandas, TensorFlow, NumPy, scikit-learn or similar) and SQLHands-on experience with gradient boosting, regression, and time-series or sequential modelingExperience designing backtests and avoiding leakage and overfittingAbility to communicate results clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholdersBachelor's degree in Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Economics, or a related quantitative fieldWillingness to be available during some nights and weekends of live games (as necessary)
Nice to Have:Experience with pricing, market making, or market microstructure in sports betting or prediction marketsA track record of building and running your own models in live marketsExperience with sports data, player tracking data, or play-by-play dataExperience deploying models to real-time or low-latency systemsExposure to AWS or GCP, Docker, and workflow orchestration tools
Benefits:Health, Vision, Dental, and Life Insurance: Comprehensive plans for all full-time employees that are HSA-eligibleUnlimited PTO: Take time off when you need it while owning your responsibilities401(k) benefitsWFH and Mental Health + Wellness stipends to support your home office setup and wellnessFlexible Hours: Flexibility around in-office days, as long as deliverables are achievedLearning and Development: Access to training, courses, and conferences to grow your skillsLive Game Tickets: Tickets to attend live sports games during the yearSubscription to Claude/Codex/Gemini Accounts
Application Process:Assessment: Complete a take-home modeling and feature engineering exercise built on real game and market data.Interview: Walk our data science team through your approach and results.Final Round: Meet leadership in person at our New York office.

rows.title: Assistant Professor-Computer Engineering
rows.descriptionText:
RIT's Department of Computer Engineering invites applications from highly motivated individuals looking to join a vibrant community of teacher-scholars as a tenure-track faculty member at the rank of Assistant Professor. Successful candidates are expected to build a strong externally-funded research program, advise Ph.D. and master's students, develop and teach undergraduate and graduate classes, advise undergraduate researchers and design teams, and work collaboratively to advance the goals of the department. We are currently seeking candidates with research expertise in one or more of the following areas: Machine Learning and Edge AI, Heterogeneous Computing, Networking and IoT, Quantum Computing.

We are seeking an individual who has the ability and interest in contributing to a community committed to student-centeredness; professional development and scholarship; integrity and ethics; respect, innovation and flexibility; and teamwork and collaboration. Select to view links to RIT's core values, honor code, and commitment to community statement.

Salary Range: $100,000 - $130,000

The College/ Department

The Computer Engineering Department is one of six academic departments in the Kate Gleason College of Engineering. The Kate Gleason College of Engineering | RIT offers bachelor's and master's in biomedical engineering, chemical engineering, computer engineering, electrical engineering, industrial engineering, mechanical engineering, and microelectronics engineering as well as four Ph.D. degrees in biomedical and chemical engineering, electrical and computer engineering, mechanical and industrial engineering, and microsystems engineering and additional master's programs in engineering management and leadership. Serving over 2600 undergraduates and 400 graduate students, the college is committed to growing its research profile while maintaining a strong commitment to undergraduate education. Major research themes include advanced manufacturing; biomedical and healthcare engineering; artificial intelligence and machine learning; cyber-physical systems; micro- and nanoscale systems devices and materials; energy and environment; and data analysis modeling and simulation. Hallmarks of the undergraduate experience include one full year of cooperative education, an innovative multidisciplinary senior design program, and an impressive variety of well-supported student teams and clubs.

The Computer Engineering Department has about four hundred and fifty undergraduates, one hundred graduate students, and eighteen faculty and staff. The department is known for its outstanding curricula, career-oriented education, collaborative research and state-of-the-art laboratories and computing facilities. Faculty members are actively engaged in research, innovative teaching, and partnerships with industry, and participate in the Electrical and Computer Engineering Ph.D. and cross-disciplinary Ph.D. programs in Computing and Information Sciences, Microsystems Engineering, and Imaging Science. For more information, visit https://www.rit.edu/kgcoe/computerengineering/.

The University And Rochester Community

Rochester Institute of Technology is home to leading creators, entrepreneurs, innovators, and researchers. The university enrolls 16,868 undergraduates and 2,904 graduate students in more than 200 programs, and across nine academic colleges, five international campuses, as well as other degree-granting units, placing it among some of the largest private universities in the U.S. RIT is internationally recognized and ranked for academic leadership in business, computing, engineering, imaging science, liberal arts, sustainability, and fine and applied arts. RIT is also home to the National Technical Institute for the Deaf, the world's first and largest technological college for deaf and hard-of-hearing students. With more than 900 students from around the world, NTID offers unparalleled support services for deaf and hard-of-hearing students. RIT's cooperative education program is one of the oldest and largest in the nation. The university revised its 2025 strategic plan, Greatness Through Difference, in the fall of 2018. The plan leverages RIT's unique history with a renewed focus on using the interdisciplinary power of technology, the arts, and design to shape the future and the world.

In 2019, RIT moved into the high research activity institution or "R2" category under the updated Carnegie Classification of Institutions of Higher Learning, ranking it among the top six percent of colleges and universities in the nation for research activity. U.S. News and World Report (USNWR) now ranks RIT No. 105 in its "National Universities" category, and No. 54 and No. 63 for Best Undergraduate and Graduate Engineering Programs, respectively. The publication also ranks RIT No. 11 in the U.S. for co-op or internship programs, No. 48 among best-value schools, and No. 41 among most innovative. Sponsored research awards totaled $92 million in the fiscal year 2022, up from $78 million in 2018. Today, RIT counts nearly 140,000 alumni around the world. Its endowment is currently valued at $1.257 billion, and the university benefits from sound financial management.

Always on the cutting edge, RIT's educational programs continue to evolve to meet the needs of today's students. Building on its legacy of excellence across STEM and the arts and its commitment to developing creative thinkers, RIT launched the Performing Arts Scholars program in 2019. In the fall of 2022, 482 first-year students accepted scholarships to join this program, regardless of major, bringing the total number of PA Scholars to 1,400. In support of this programming, RIT is unveiling the Student Hall for Exploration and Development (SHED) in the fall of 2023, with major facilities for the performing arts, and new classrooms, surrounding an enormous multi-story core of maker spaces. RIT has also launched a series of very successful Combined Accelerated Bachelor's/Master's Degree (CAB-M) programs, which attracted about 750 students in the fall of 2022. In addition, RIT is developing a large suite of online programs with an emphasis on upskilling for adult learners through its offerings at RIT Certified.

Qualifications

 Doctorate in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering or closely related fieldAbility and commitment to effectively teach and mentor undergraduate and graduate students Record of disseminating scholarly research in refereed (peer-reviewed) publications Demonstrated evidence of experience or potential to establish an independent externally-sponsored research programExpertise in the areas of Edge AI, Heterogeneous Computing, Networking and IoT, and/or Quantum Computing.Excellent communication skillsAbility to contribute in meaningful ways to the university's continuing commitment to cultural diversity, pluralism and individual differences.Interest in working in a collaborative, collegial environment

Join Cantor Fitzgerald Technology Markets LLC as a Machine Learning Engineer focused on building AI‑driven solutions for a high‑volume financial services business. You will work closely with product, engineering, and business teams to create, test, and operationalize large language model (LLM) applications, ensuring they meet performance, reliability, and responsible‑AI standards.

 Design and implement LLM‑driven features in production systems. Build and maintain data pipelines for both structured and unstructured data. Overview

 JOB DESCRIPTION 

The Jefferies Equity Research Data Strategy Team is a global team embedded within the Equity Research department, responsible for shaping and executing the department's data and AI strategy. On the data side, the team helps incorporate fundamental and alternative datasets into Analyst research reports, combining analysts’ domain expertise with our team’s technical skills to produce thoughtful, defensible, and actionable analysis of real-world behavior at scale. On the AI side, our team is responsible for building internal generative AI tooling along with evaluating third-party AI models and tools to enhance our analysts’ work. We help integrate AI capabilities into analysts’ daily workflows and ensure that first- and third-party datasets are fully AI-accessible to them. Statistics, data engineering, data science, and AI are cornerstones of our work.

As a Data Scientist at Jefferies, your focus will be to support the Research Analysts and the Data Strategy Team’s broader platform. The candidate will use technical and financial skills to implement ideas and requests from the Research Analysts, while also building and maintaining relationships with internal and external stakeholders, working in collaboration with the rest of the Global Data Strategy Team.

Key Responsibilities

 Query, transform, analyze, and combine large datasets in support of solving problems and implementing research ideas across sectors and data categories, occasionally developing statistical models to predict outcomes  Enhance our platform through the creation and maintenance of tools, AI agents, MCP servers, and processes that streamline, scale, and standardize our ability to evaluate, clean, analyze, and disseminate data  Contribute to the data centralization process, ensuring all first- and third-party data assets are AI-accessible and meet quality, lineage, and governance standards  Present highly technical methods to non-technical stakeholders and translate open-ended questions into data-driven insights  Maintain and build relationships with key internal and external stakeholders, including research teams, third-party data vendors, management, and possibly buy-side clients 

Qualifications

Required

 Transferable experience on the sell-side or buy-side, in data science, data research, or similar function  STEM degree with preference for Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, Statistics, Quantitative Finance, and related disciplines  Strong proficiency with Python, intermediate or better proficiency with SQL and/or Apache Spark  Experience analyzing and visualizing large datasets  Experience with AI-assisted development (Claude Code, GitHub CoPilot, Cursor, etc.)  Familiarity with LLMs, LangChain, vector databases, and RAG pipelines  Excellent communication skills with the ability to translate complex technical concepts for non-technical stakeholders 

Preferred

 Demonstrated interest in fundamental equity research and financial modelling  Experience with Databricks or Snowflake and cloud platforms such as AWS  Experience with Atlassian project management tools (JIRA, Confluence, Bitbucket)  Experience with knowledge graphs 

Primary Location Full Time Salary Range of $100,000 - $120,000.

Jefferies is a leading global, full-service investment banking and capital markets firm that provides advisory, sales and trading, research, and wealth and asset management services.
